Danielle — thanks for the MAP and the timeline. Quick summary to include in your procurement note and the MAP: 

1) Baseline tokens/$ assumption we used in the workbook:
   - Model: redwood/gptx-13b (quantized)
   - Baseline throughput profile: median request length 120 tokens, response length 220 tokens
   - Baseline tokens per dollar (hosted tier, no caching): ~27,000 tokens/$ (this includes average latency/throughput mix)

2) Caching & batching impact (short version for MAP):
   - Prefix/KV caching (session-level prefix reuse) can reduce token generation by 20–55% for conversational flows that re-use prompts/KB snippets. We recommend planning a conservative 25% cache uplift for evaluation planning.
   - Continuous batching (server-side batching across concurrent requests) reduces per-token cost by improving GPU utilization; practical savings show ~10–18% on tokens/$ for steady traffic. For spike tests, batching gains are lower unless requests are buffered (we do an adaptive short-batch window to preserve latency).

3) Sensitivity bands we recommend capturing in the MAP: 
   - Pessimistic: no caching, burst unbatched traffic => ~18,000 tokens/$
   - Base: conservative caching (25%) + typical batching => ~33,750 tokens/$
   - Optimistic: heavy cache reuse (50%) + ideal batching => ~48,600 tokens/$

4) For your 2-week eval w/ 5k DAU spike: assume the spike week will be closer to the pessimistic band for the first 24–48 hours, then move toward base as caches warm and traffic patterns stabilize. Plan an uplift contingency of ~25% on budget for the spike.

I'll flag Ben on the technical caching/batching notes below with specific config suggestions you can surface in your SOW.

Next steps I propose before procurement signoff: 
- We update the MAP with the short tokens/$ sensitivity paragraph (I'll submit a tracked change).
- Ben and Monica to confirm the SOW clause for caching behavior and acceptance criteria for the eval (latency SLOs, accepted token variance).

Thanks — I'll aim to send the tracked MAP by tomorrow EOD.

Best,
Priya

Danielle / team — quick technical clarifications to make the MAP actionable (these are the bits we ask to include in the SOW / eval plan):

- Cache types: we provide two layers — prefix-level (prompt dedup/short-term reuse) and KV cache (decoder-state reuse across turns). For a conversational pilot, KV cache yields the largest token savings after warmup. Specify KV cache retention policy (we typically recommend session TTL 30–60m for evaluation).

- Batching config recommended for your profile: adaptive batching with a 12–25ms micro-batch window and a 40-request soft cap per batch. That balances latency (99th p95 target ~160–220ms depending on model) and utilization. If you require p95 < 120ms, reduce batch window and expect batching savings to drop by ~8–12 percentage points.

- Measurement: define a canonical eval traffic trace (sample of 1k users, representative queries) that we both run in week 0 (dry run). We'll log token counts, cache hit rates, and per-route latency. Acceptance criterion for evaluation: cache hit rate > 20% by day 3 and token usage within the base sensitivity band +/- 15%.

- Artifacts for SOW: add a short appendix stating the token accounting method (server-side counted model output tokens + request tokens) and that final invoices reconcile to observed token usage during the pilot window with an agreed reconciliation window (30 days).

I can draft the technical appendix and include the config snippet for adaptive batching. Priya — if you want, I’ll push the appendix into the SOW-draft-Redwood.pdf and send back for procurement redline.

Ben
